mechanism_chain.detail: plant age, ownership, rents, safety regulation, bargaining coverage

mechanism_chain.link: establishment premium -> within-occupation wage gap across generation industries
mechanism_chain.detail: observed in OEWS occupation-by-industry cells; moderated by occupation group and time

hypotheses.text: Within detailed occupations and years, mean hourly wages in renewable generation industries are lower than in non-renewable (fossil fuel and nuclear) generation industries.
hypotheses.mechanism: establishment rent-sharing and wage-setting institutions stronger in legacy generation
hypotheses.scope: US NAICS 2211 generation industries, detailed occupations, 2021-2025

hypotheses.text: Differences in occupational composition account for part, but not all, of the raw renewable/non-renewable gap in mean hourly wages.
hypotheses.direction: partial attenuation (raw gap differs from within-occupation gap but within-occupation gap remains nonzero)

hypotheses.text: Relative to fossil fuel generation and within occupations, nuclear generation pays more, hydroelectric generation pays about the same, and solar and wind generation pay less.
hypotheses.direction: nuclear positive; hydro null; solar and wind negative
hypotheses.mechanism: institutional maturity, regulation and bargaining coverage by source

hypotheses.text: The within-occupation renewable wage penalty is larger in production, installation, maintenance, and repair occupations than in management, business, and professional occupations.
hypotheses.direction: larger negative gap in plant-based occupations
hypotheses.moderator: occupational group (bargaining coverage and labor-market scope)
hypotheses.mechanism: establishment premia matter most for occupations paid inside plant job ladders

hypotheses.text: The within-occupation renewable/non-renewable wage gap narrows between 2021 and 2025.
hypotheses.direction: gap shrinks toward zero over time
hypotheses.mechanism: segment maturation, rising union representation, IRA prevailing-wage standards

gap_statement: Economy-wide studies report green premia while direct clean-vs-legacy comparisons find parity or a legacy advantage; no study compares the same occupations across renewable and non-renewable generation within one industry, or tracks such gaps through 2021-2025.
novelty_contrast: Unlike Curtis and Marinescu (2023), wages are industry-specific rather than economy-wide occupational medians; unlike Colmer et al. (2025) and Godoy and Isaksen (2025), comparison is within detailed occupation across generation sources for 2021-2025.

journal_calibration.theory_depth: compact framework (about 1,600 words) contrasting legacy rent-sharing with green skills-scarcity and compensating-differential accounts
journal_calibration.citation_density: about 34 sources in literature section; policy-relevant energy and labor economics sources prioritized
journal_calibration.must_cite_strategy: cite all nine user-supplied studies with strengths/weaknesses, core firm-premium theory, and US energy-employment context
